title: Briefly gap-junction-blocked planaria make other species' heads, then revert

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Briefly gap-junction-blocked planaria make other species' heads, then revert

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Planaria briefly treated with a gap-junction blocker regenerate heads shaped like those of other planarian species but eventually remodel back to their correct species-specific target morphology, which the author takes as parallel to the temporary loss and return of the Self under anesthesia.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Consciousness

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Interestingly, and in line with the proposed isomorphism between cognition and morphogenesis, gap junction blockade has exactly this effect in regeneration: planaria briefly treated with GJ blocker regenerate heads of other species, but eventually snap out of it and remodel back to their correct target morphology (Emmons-Bell et al., 2015).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Consciousness”. Scope: Girardia dorotocephala planarian fragments treated with octanol

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-33: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Transient cross-species-like morphology and subsequent reversion are directly testable from longitudinal images. Existing studies can resolve the anatomical observation, while the proposed parallel to loss and return of Self remains conceptual.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify head-shape trajectories after transient gap-junction blockade, classify early heads against reference species, and test whether untreated longitudinal remodeling returns them toward the original species centroid.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cross-species resemblance depends on morphometric reference sets.

Complete longitudinal raw images may not be public.

The anesthesia analogy is not tested by morphology alone.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.92
data adequacy: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Species-likeness scores over time are a direct test, and the octanol study publishes morphometrics and a later return to Girardia shape for this protocol. Planform can hold curated morphology outcomes and does not replace those landmarks. The shape time course can be audited from the paper, and the analogy to loss and return of a Self under anesthesia is not an additional empirical result in the data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After a brief octanol exposure, classify regenerated Girardia head shape against reference species at the end of regeneration and again weeks later; the morphological claim holds if non-native shapes are enriched early and then return to the species-typical shape.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Landmark coordinates and time courses live in the 2015 paper and its supplement, not as a confirmed open morphometric file.

Planform may store categorical outcomes rather than the remodeling trajectory.

The parallel with anesthesia is an interpretation and is not tested by head shape.
